podcasts.excerpt: AI is changing how content is created, software is built, and risk management decisions are supported. But easier creation does not automatically mean better outcomes. The real challenge is preserving human judgment while grounding AI in trusted data and rigorous evaluation. In this episode, Han Lee , Senior Director of Data and AI at Moody’s, joins host Alex Pillow . Together they cut through the AI hype to explore what makes AI genuinely useful, trustworthy, and practical in risk management, from authentic writing and AI-enabled engineering to evaluation, trusted data, and total cost of ownership. Key topics include: Why AI-generated content can converge toward a similar voice, and the importance of preserving original thinking and human expression How AI coding agents are shifting engineering bottlenecks from writing code toward deciding, planning, reviewing, and coordinating work Why domain expertise, trusted data, evaluation, monitoring, and auditability matter for AI used in risk and compliance How to think about build versus buy through total cost of ownership, including ongoing software, data, and operational maintenance Additional resources: Han's new book: LLM Evaluation and Alignment, The Foundational Ideas Visit moodys.com to learn more Hosted by Simplecast, an AdsWizz company. podcasts.excerpt: The fight against financial crime is entering a new era shaped by AI, evolving criminal networks, and growing demands for faster, more effective investigations. As organizations grapple with fragmented data, emerging threats, and increasing regulatory scrutiny, success depends on combining technology, trusted intelligence, and human expertise. In this episode, Katie Jackson , UK Head of Forensic at Deloitte and Francis Marinier , Industry Practice Lead at Moody’s, join host Alex Pillow to explore how financial crime investigations are evolving and what organizations are doing today to prepare for the future. Together, they discuss how AI, agentic technologies, data strategies, and cross-functional collaboration can impact the detection, investigation, and prevention of financial crime. Key topics covered: Why financial crime threats are becoming more sophisticated, faster, and harder to detect in a digital-first world The shift from siloed fraud and AML functions toward more integrated risk and investigation models What “investigation-grade intelligence” means and why trusted, connected data is foundational to effective investigations How AI agents help automate data gathering, so investigators can focus on analysis, judgment, and critical thinking The growing importance of governance, explainability, and data lineage in AI-driven investigations Recommended resources: Deloitte website Deloitte Future of FinCrime series Moody’s blogs: Breaking the spell of global fraud: The role of counterparty data https://www.moodys.com/web/en/us/insights/ai/connected-intelligence-decision-grade-ai-delivered-whe… Visit moodys.com to learn more.
